findings.evidence: Page 49: "~5.7B per expert × 8 = 45.6B + ~1.4B always-on (attention/shared + embeddings) = 47B" — arithmetic check: 45.6 + 1.4 = 47.0B ✓. However the same page also states "~12.8B active per token" and derives it as "2 × 5.7B routed experts + ~1.4B always-on = 12.8B". Check: 2 × 5.7 = 11.4; 11.4 + 1.4 = 12.8B ✓. Then it says "~27% of total" as 12.8/47 = 27.23% ✓. All arithmetic checks out. But page 44 Table 3-2 says the active fraction for top-2-of-8 is "~24–27%" while the derivation column on the same row states "~27%". The ~24% lower bound comes from counting expert-FFN mass alone (11.4/47 = 24.3%) which is stated, so this is internally consistent but potentially confusing without closer reading.
findings.issue: The ~24–27% range for top-2-of-8 active/total fraction is stated in one cell but the derivation column only shows the ~27% end. While both values are derivable from stated inputs (11.4/47 ≈ 24.3% and 12.8/47 ≈ 27.2%), the derivation column does not explain the ~24% lower bound, leaving the range's provenance partially implicit.
findings.fix_instruction: In Table 3-2's active/total fraction row, add the ~24% derivation (11.4B ÷ 47B ≈ 24.3%, expert-FFN mass alone) alongside the existing ~27% figure so the stated range is fully traceable from the derivation column.

findings.evidence: Page 56, Figure 3.4 caption: "inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)" — check: 6 × 11.4 = 68.4 GB ✓. Caption also says "active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)" — check: 2 × 11.4 = 22.8 GB, displayed as ≈23 GB ✓. Caption says "MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on" — check: 91 + 3 = 94 ✓, and 8 × 11.4 = 91.2 ≈ 91 ✓, and 1.4B × 2B = 2.8 ≈ 3 ✓. Arithmetic all correct. However the caption states "1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)" — check: 5.7B × 2 = 11.4B bytes = 11.4 GB ✓. All arithmetic verified correct.
findings.issue: No arithmetic defect found — all figure 3.4 values recompute correctly from the stated inputs.

findings.evidence: Page 57, Table 3-3: "KV cache per request (9.2K ctx, FP16): dense 70B ~24.1 GB, MoE ~1.2 GB" — derivation states "dense 80L/8192H full-MHA = 2.62 MB/token × 9,200 ≈ 24.1 GB" ✓ (2.62144 × 9200 = 24,117 MB ≈ 24.1 GB). For MoE: "the challenger's own 32L/4096H GQA (8 KV-heads × 128) = 0.131 MB/token × 9,200 ≈ 1.20 GB" — check: 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131,072 B = 0.131072 MB/token; 0.131 × 9200 = 1,205 MB ≈ 1.20 GB ✓. However the table cell says "~1.2 GB" while the derivation says "≈ 1.20 GB" — these are consistent (1.2 vs 1.20). But page 46 (Ch 3 §3.3.3) states the same MoE KV as "~1.2 GB at FP16" while Table 3-3 on p.57 states "~1.2 GB" — consistent. However page 46 says the Mixtral KV per token at 8-bit is "0.0655 MB/token" and gives total as "~0.60 GB" while Table 3-3 on p.57 says "~0.60 GB" — consistent. Cross-checking: 0.065536 × 9200 = 603 MB ≈ 0.60 GB ✓. All values consistent across pages.
findings.issue: Cross-chapter consistency check on KV figures passes — no contradiction found between p.46, p.57 Table 3-3, and p.79 Table 4-2 for the dense 70B KV values.
findings.fix_instruction: No fix needed; values verified consistent.

findings.evidence: Page 43, Table 3-1: "FLOPs per token (batch-1 decode forward pass, approx.): ~0.14T — 70B × 2 FLOP/param (multiply-add = 2 FLOPs, Ch 8)". Check: 70 × 10⁹ × 2 = 140 × 10⁹ = 0.14T ✓. Table 3-2 (p.44): "FLOPs per token (batch-1 decode forward pass, approx.): ~0.0256T — 12.8B active × 2 FLOP/param = 25.6B". Check: 12.8 × 10⁹ × 2 = 25.6 × 10⁹ = 0.0256T ✓. "compute ratio vs dense 70B: ~0.183× (12.8B × 2) ÷ (70B × 2) = 25.6 GFLOP ÷ 140 GFLOP ≈ 0.183×". Check: 25.6/140 = 0.1829 ≈ 0.183 ✓. "the canonical 70B dense baseline costs about 5.5× the compute per token". Check: 140/25.6 = 5.47 ≈ 5.5 ✓. "against a same-total (47B) dense model the saving is 3.7× (12.8B ÷ 47B ≈ 27%)". Check: 47/12.8 = 3.67 ≈ 3.7 ✓. All correct.
findings.issue: No arithmetic defect — MoE vs dense FLOP ratios and compute savings recompute correctly against both baselines.

findings.evidence: PDF p.73 (printed p.49): "Qwen3.8-27B ([1P][FACT], model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B is a dense 27.8B model whose 4-bit weights fit on a single 24 GB consumer GPU, and Muse Glimmer 30B ([2°][FACT], source: vLLM-Recipes, citing the Meta model card) is a dense 29.6B local-agentic model...". The parenthesis opened after "Qwen3.8-27B (" is never closed; the only closing paren on the sentence belongs to the Muse Glimmer citation. Parallel citation parentheticals in the same chapter close correctly (e.g. §3.3.2: "...https://mistral.ai/news/mixtral-of-experts/ retrieved 2026-11-23)"), so this is not an extraction artifact pattern.
findings.issue: Malformed citation: unclosed parenthesis makes the evidence tag, URL and the following claim read as one parenthetical, so the sentence "is a dense 27.8B model..." appears to sit inside the citation.
findings.fix_instruction: Close the parenthetical immediately after the model-card URL: "Qwen3.8-27B ([1P][FACT], model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) is a dense 27.8B model whose 4-bit weights fit on a single 24 GB consumer GPU...".
